text:
Jason Robertson signed a one-year deal with Dallas, and the noise around it hasn't stopped: Seattle's interest, Jim Nill's next contract test, a hat trick in 5:20 against Washington that was the third fastest in franchise history. Every Robertson headline is really a question about how long this core stays together.

On the ice, the Stars are 10-5-2 and quietly sturdy. They have allowed 2.29 goals a game, and their goalies have stopped about eight more than the chances against them would predict, which says a lot about Jake Oettinger's season. The offense is the opposite: 4.7 goals fewer than expected, so some of the scoring should come back. Mikko Rantanen's line with Wyatt Johnston and Sam Steel has taken 67 percent of the expected goals together.

Two things to watch. Miro Heiskanen left Tuesday with an upper-body injury and was listed day to day; Dallas without him is a different defense. And Jamie Benn sat two points from 1,000 after Tuesday's game, set to join Mike Modano as the only players in Stars and North Stars history to get there. Our simulations give Dallas an 86 percent playoff chance. The penalty count, 4.12 taken a game against 3.18 drawn, is the habit we'd want fixed first.
headline: Dallas wins with defense and waits on Robertson's future
